A later current-build INIT descriptor scan then found the matching value-name binding row pointing at the same live global RVA, which closes the static registry-seeding layer for the candidate. A new host-driven KVM reboot observation then confirmed that the `Control\Power` parent key still exists across a real guest reboot while `Win32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds` stays absent before and after boot. A dedicated KVM S1 Procmon replay reached live guest execution through a new `watchdog-s1-callout` trigger; a cleanup rerun removed stale Procmon boot-log registry state before capture, but Procmon `SaveAs` still timed out before any CSV review. A later non-Procmon S1 ETW lane produced a real registry ETL with sentinel hits but no target read during the bounded S1 window. This is a stronger current-build lead than the bugcheck-enabled sibling, but the exact runtime registry read and non-default override semantics are still unproven.

setting.name: Win32k Callout Watchdog Timeout Seconds
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a low-level power-manager watchdog timeout for Win32k callouts. On the observed clean baseline the registry value is not configured, but the running kernel still keeps an in-memory default.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel and power researchers may inspect this value when tracing Win32k callout watchdog behavior and watchdog packet timing in the power manager.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The candidate now has repo routing, clean-baseline absence, exact current-build string presence, a live current-build consumer path, a current-build INIT descriptor binding for the same global, a reboot-backed confirmation that the `Control\Power` parent key survives a real guest reboot while the value stays absent, dedicated KVM S1 Procmon attempts, and a non-Procmon S1 ETW no-hit with sentinel validation. It is still too weak for a published tweak because exact runtime registry-read proof and non-default override semantics remain unresolved, and the current evidence suggests the registry read is not occurring during the bounded S1 trigger window.
setting.professional_notes: The repo docs-first power routing pass already listed `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Power\\Win32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds` as a new candidate. A later existence-first pass on the observed clean baseline confirmed that the `Control\\Power` path exists while the value itself is absent. A later targeted current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `Win32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds` in `C:\\Windows\\System32\\ntoskrnl.exe`. A later KVM local-KD follow-up then resolved the live current-build watchdog-family cluster around `PopInvokeWin32CalloutWithWatchdog` and directly read `PopWin32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds = 0x1e` (`30`). The same pass disassembled `PopInvokeWin32CalloutWithWatchdog` and showed a direct `imul` against the global by `1000`, followed by the watchdog packet path through `ZwPowerInformation` and the surrounding Win32 callout path. That is materially stronger than a string-only or sibling-only clue: the running kernel is actively consuming the global even though the registry value is missing on the observed baseline. The main open question is whether the registry value is an optional override on top of a built-in 30-second default, or whether a boot-only helper still seeds the same global from `Control\\Power` when present. A later host-side current-build INIT descriptor scan found the `Win32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds` UTF-16 string in `ntoskrnl.exe` and one nearby row at file offset `0xbee0e8` pointing at static RVA `0xE0B518`, matching the live KD RVA for `nt!PopWin32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds`. The nearest retained key-context string in that row family is the generic `Power` label rather than a longer decoded `Control\Power` path, but the row/global alignment is still current-build specific and closes the static registry-seeding layer. A later host-driven KVM reboot observation then advanced the guest boot time from `2026-04-12T04:20:14.5000000Z` to `2026-04-12T04:33:01.5000000Z` while `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Power` stayed present and `Win32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds` stayed absent before and after reboot. That closed the reboot-diff story for this candidate. A later KVM follow-up then added a dedicated `watchdog-s1-callout` Procmon trigger, reached live guest execution, and preserved the missing-value baseline, but Procmon first surfaced stale boot-time-log UI and then exited `SaveAs` with code `1` before it produced any CSV. A cleanup rerun cleared stale Procmon boot residue before capture, removing the previous `Logfile`, `SourcePath`, and `FlightRecorder` state under `HKCU:\\Software\\Sysinternals\\Process Monitor`; no stale bootlog files were present and no cleanup errors were reported. That rerun avoided the earlier stale boot-log modal but still timed out in `Procmon SaveAs` after 180 seconds with no CSV or normalized bundle, while again restoring the missing-value baseline. The newest non-Procmon ETW follow-up used `Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Registry` around the same `watchdog-s1-callout` trigger. The successful pass produced a 2,867,200-byte ETL, guest-side `tracerpt` completed, and a non-target sentinel query produced 50 XML hits, proving the provider/parser path was live. No target hits for `Win32kCalloutWatchdogTimeoutSeconds` or `Control\Power` appeared during the bounded S1 window. The next runtime attempt should shift toward boot-time registry seeding or a more targeted WPR/KD lane rather than another Procmon GUI export replay.
